title: Unique Visitors
story: Your website analytics dashboard shows 10,000 page views today. But how many of those are from unique visitors? If one person refreshes the page 50 times, that's 50 page views but only 1 visitor. You need to count unique users efficiently.
why: Tracking unique visitors with Set is a classic real-world pattern — count the total (Vec) vs count the unique (Set) to measure engagement.
analogy: Unique visitor tracking is like a concert venue's clicker vs guest list. The clicker (Vec count) goes up every time the door opens — that's your page views. The guest list (Set) only records each person once — that's your unique visitors. A venue with 500 clicker counts but only 100 names on the list means people are coming and going a lot.
try_it: Add a 'new vs returning' counter: count how many visitors are first-timers (not yet in the Set when they arrive) vs returning (already in the Set). Track the timestamp of each visitor's first visit using a Map alongside the Set. Calculate the bounce rate: visitors who only visited once divided by total unique visitors.
tips: Use a Vec alongside a Set — Vec preserves order and total count, Set guarantees uniqueness
Set's `.len()` tells you how many UNIQUE items, Vec's `.len()` tells you TOTAL items
The ratio of unique to total (unique / total) measures how much repetition is in your data
common_mistakes: Only using a Set and losing total visit count — Set can't tell you how many times someone visited
Using a Set for ordered data — Set doesn't preserve insertion order; use Vec for ordering
Checking if someone visited by scanning the Vec — O(n); use Set.contains() for O(1)
